answer.generated: The formula to calculate the number of processors with the highest speedup in such an application can be derived by considering the balance between parallelizable time and communication overhead. Let \( n \) represent the number of processors, \( T_0 \) the original execution time, and \( P \) the percentage of the original execution time that is parallelizable. The speedup \( S(n) \) is maximized when the ratio of parallelizable time to communication overhead is optimal, leading to the equation \( S(n) = \frac{P \cdot T_0}{(1 - 0.005^n) \cdot T_0} \), where the denominator accounts for the cumulative increase in communication time as the number of processors is doubled.
